scope_note: This is the generation-11 corrective pass responding to the independent Codex reviewer's rejection of PR #5620 exact head 560661230adff50137f9bac0f5564afc910c24d1 (frozen manifest blob 0f41f29d3e64033815b1e61abfbce6bfb7c815ba). Each of the 6 findings is fixed with real code changes: (1) allocation-policy-artifacts POST supplied-registry_id collision bypassed authorization and kind/content validation, letting a cross-tenant caller (or same-tenant caller targeting a different artifact kind, e.g. a private StrategySpec) read the colliding row unconditionally -- register_allocation_policy_artifact now calls RegistryService.register_if_absent instead of the plain register(), and on a collision (created=False) authorizes the returned view (_authorize_read, tenant/builtin scoped) and validates its kind/content against the caller's own request (new _ensure_alloc_policy_registration_matches) before ever returning it, mirroring the StrategySpec/StrategyArtifact facades' existing pattern. (2) create_with_receipt (the Idempotency-Key'd POST /api/registry/entries path) acquired its receipts-table SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock before ever touching entries, the opposite order from create_if_absent/register_strategy_spec_revision/commit_metadata_cas/commit_artifact_state_cas (all of which touch entries before receipts) -- two unrelated, lawful concurrent HTTP requests on opposite paths could deadlock in Postgres. Added PostgresJsonOwnerStore.lock_table (services/foundation/postgres_json_store.py) so every method that writes to both tables in one transaction can explicitly acquire the entries lock first, before any receipts access; create_with_receipt, commit_metadata_cas, and commit_artifact_state_cas all now do this, making the acquisition order globally consistent (entries always before receipts). (3) StrategyCommandAdapter.update_params trusted a replay response's own self-reported actor_id (any non-empty value, not necessarily the actual caller's), and a normal (non-replay) response's null commit timestamp/absent actor slipped through when a follow-up readback happened to be equally null/absent; an ambiguous/empty PATCH body recovered via a follow-up readback could be reported success purely because the target metadata already matched *before* the command ever ran, with no signal distinguishing a real commit from a pre-existing value. Fixed by: deriving the caller's own verified actor identity locally from its auth_token (new _resolve_caller_actor_id, mirroring command_executor.py's _extract_actor_id) and cross-checking it against a replay's last_actor.actor_id with no extra network call (preserving the existing 'no third HTTP call on replay' contract); requiring a non-null updated_at on the normal (non-replay) response path; and requiring the ambiguous-response-recovery readback's updated_at to differ from the pre-mutation baseline captured before the PATCH was ever issued, plus a recorded actor, as proof this specific command actually committed a change. (4) a typed create-if-absent replay (StrategySpec/StrategyArtifact/AllocationPolicyArtifact facades) returned the entry's *current* (possibly since-mutated by an unrelated later command) fields instead of the original creation snapshot recorded by get_creation_receipt -- the prior generation deliberately kept this to avoid conflating 'reverting live state' with 'what this POST call reports as its own result', but the reviewer clarified these are different: a caller retrying its own create command expects back exactly what that command committed, not a later unrelated command's edit. All three facades (_ensure_strategy_spec_registration_matches, _register_strategy_artifact, _ensure_alloc_policy_registration_matches) now return the original creation-receipt view when one is recorded; the ordinary GET route is unaffected and still returns live state. (5) AdvanceRequest's expected_artifact_state/expected_version/expected_updated_at were all optional, so a caller could omit every claimed-base field and the CAS silently fell back to a freshly server-read current row -- not a CAS at all. expected_artifact_state is now a required field on every public advance facade (POST .../advance for entries, strategy-specs, strategy-artifacts, and allocation-policy-artifacts); FastAPI rejects an omitted value with 422 before any mutation is attempted. (6) evidence/test completeness -- new regression tests were added for every finding above (see files_modified), including a real 8-way-concurrent mixed keyed/unkeyed create proof for finding 2 (asserts no raw 500/uncaught deadlock, only ordinary 200/409 outcomes), and the two BFF test files that previously failed to even collect (test_command_executor.py, tests/test_command_adapters_router.py) are now fixed and passing -- both used a stale sys.path.insert + bare top-level module import style that collided with services/control_plane/bff/__init__.py's namespace-package extension (which exposes the on-disk 'control-plane' directory as services.control_plane.bff); switched to the canonical services.control_plane.bff.<module> import path already used by every other passing test in these directories, and updated one test (test_typed_domain_command_dispatch_and_receipt) that was asserting the intentionally-removed fabricated submit_review success behavior, plus one test-isolation fix (a shared main.command_store singleton's file_path leaking between two regression tests) that surfaced once collection started succeeding.

summary: service.py: register_allocation_policy_artifact now uses register_if_absent + a new _ensure_alloc_policy_registration_matches (authorize-then-content-match-then-return-original-snapshot) instead of the plain register() (finding 1); _ensure_strategy_spec_registration_matches and _register_strategy_artifact now return the original creation-receipt view (when recorded) instead of the live current view on an exact-content replay (finding 4); AdvanceRequest.expected_artifact_state changed from Optional[ArtifactState]=None to a required ArtifactState field (finding 5).

postgres_json_store.py: new PostgresJsonOwnerStore.lock_table(conn=...) acquires this table's SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock standalone, with no insert, so a caller writing to two tables in one transaction can pin a consistent global acquisition order (finding 2).

pg_store.py: create_with_receipt, commit_metadata_cas, and commit_artifact_state_cas each call self._entries.lock_table(conn=conn) before ever touching receipts in the same transaction, matching create_if_absent/register_strategy_spec_revision's existing entries-then-receipts order (finding 2).

review.decision: The prior head (560661230adff50137f9bac0f5564afc910c24d1) was rejected via GitHub reopen with 6 concrete, live-PostgreSQL-reproduced defects: an allocation-policy-artifacts POST authorization/content-validation bypass on a caller-supplied registry_id collision, an inconsistent cross-table Postgres lock order that could deadlock mixed create paths, three distinct StrategyCommandAdapter false-success fabrication gaps (replay actor, missing commit time, ambiguous-response no-op), a typed create replay returning the later mutated row instead of the original creation receipt, and an advance CAS that still allowed an entirely unbound request. This revision implements real fixes for all 6, verified against a live isolated PostgreSQL instance available in this session (not skipped), with new regression tests proving each fix, the reviewer's own reproduction probes re-run and confirmed no longer reproducing the defects, and no regression in the pre-existing suite (previously-uncollectable BFF executor/router tests now collect and pass too). Pending independent re-review; no reuse of any prior approval.
